chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Muqatil ibn Suleyman, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'What was the height of Adam (peace be upon him) when he was descended to the earth, and what was the height of Hawwa (peace be upon her)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'We found in the Book of Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon him) that when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, descended Adam and his wife Hawwa (peace be upon her) to the earth, his feet were at the twin peaks of Al-Safa and his head was below the horizon of the sky. And he complained to Allah from the heat of the sun that was befalling him. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Jibraeel (peace be upon him):
ai.seo_question: What was the original height of Adam and Hawwa before they were compressed on earth?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the primordial grandeur of Adam (AS) by linking his physical dimensions to the sacred geography of Mecca, specifically Mount Safa, thereby establishing a theological connection between the first human and the holiest site in Islam. It further illustrates the divine mercy in adjusting human physiology to earthly conditions, as recorded in the *Kitab Ali* tradition, emphasizing the transition from a celestial to a terrestrial existence.
